rounds.title: Hospital Operations Analytics Interview
rounds.description: Advanced interview practice on synthetic patient-flow operations, capacity planning and executive communication. No diagnosis or treatment advice.

questions.context: The interviewer gives you aggregate unit-day operations data and asks for a waiting-time comparison.
questions.prompt: Using hospital_daily_ops, return unit and ROUND(AVG(avg_wait_minutes), 1) AS avg_wait_minutes grouped by unit.
questions.explanation: A strong answer works at the aggregate unit-day grain and does not imply patient-level or clinical conclusions.

questions.context: Saturday expected arrivals are higher than planned capacity in the synthetic forecast.
options: Treat the gap as an operations-planning signal, validate forecast error and test staffing or scheduling scenarios before rollout
The forecast proves every Saturday will exceed capacity
Ignore forecast uncertainty because the point estimate is enough
questions.expectedAnswer: Treat the gap as an operations-planning signal, validate forecast error and test staffing or scheduling scenarios before rollout
questions.explanation: Forecasts support planning under uncertainty; they are not certainty statements or clinical recommendations.

questions.context: Emergency waiting time increased on two observed days. Leadership asks whether the process change failed.
questions.prompt: Describe how you would structure the analysis before making an operations recommendation.

criteria.label: Use comparable cohorts or day types

questions.explanation: A strong hospital-operations case separates demand, capacity and process effects, uses comparable periods, and recommends a controlled operational test rather than a clinical conclusion.
